identification.title: Across the Lands
identification.notes: Written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend; published by ThankYou Music; CCLI 3709898; listings give a 2002 copyright date. Also known by its opening line. Original key C per Worship Together. The Gettys' recording appears on In Christ Alone and on the live Gospel Coalition album; the album and year are taken from catalogue listings seen in search results. The list's artist guess is right for the recording churches know, but the song is a Getty and Townend co-write. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: Four verses, each ending in the same two-line refrain, which is doubled at the close; no separate bridge. Verse one declares Christ as the eternal Word through whom creation holds together. Verse two narrates the incarnation and humility, leaving heaven for the cross, with healing miracles and silent suffering for the guilty. Verse three proclaims the resurrection, ascension, intercession and the gathering of sinners from every tribe and nation. The refrain declares him creator and Lord of all and tells of his love reaching the world. Addressed to Christ throughout; the refrain widens to the whole world. The Spirit is not reached.

claims.claim: Christ is the eternal Word through whom creation was made and holds together.
claims.subject: Deity of Christ and creation

claims.claim: The Son left heaven in humility, took on flesh, healed and calmed the storm, and went silently to the cross for the guilty.
claims.subject: Incarnation and atonement

claims.claim: Christ rose, ascended and intercedes for his people.
claims.subject: Resurrection, ascension, intercession

claims.claim: Sinners from every tribe and nation are gathered to him.
claims.subject: Universal mission

claims.claim: Christ is Lord of all, and his love is carried to the world.
claims.subject: Lordship and mission

strengths.title: The eternal Word and Creator
strengths.explanation: Verse one states plainly that Christ is the Word through whom all things were made and are held together - a clear affirmation of his deity and lordship.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Word with God, through whom all things were made.

strengths.title: The sweep of Christ's life and work
strengths.explanation: Verses two and three move from incarnation and humility through the cross, resurrection, ascension and intercession, so Christ's whole work is sung in order.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Son humbling himself to death on a cross.

strengths.title: Redeemed from every nation
strengths.explanation: The third verse looks to sinners gathered from every tribe and nation, and the refrain carries his love to the world, giving the song a missionary reach.
strengths.scriptureRationale: People from every tribe and nation ransomed by his blood.

strengths.title: The ascended Christ pleads for his people
strengths.explanation: Naming ascension and intercession is rarer than naming the cross and resurrection, and it grounds ongoing assurance.

doctrinesAffirmed: The deity of Christ as eternal Word
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. The song confesses Christ as eternal Word and Lord, then follows his incarnation, death, rising, ascension and intercession. The healing and storm references are narrative of his earthly ministry, not claims needing qualification. The Spirit is not reached, and the cross is told briefly beside the larger sweep.

strengths.title: Steady melody and a returning refrain
strengths.explanation: A steady, very singable melody and a refrain that follows each verse make the song easy for a room to learn.

strengths.title: Fits a Christ-centred or missions service
strengths.explanation: The sweep of Christ's life and the world-wide refrain suit a service on the person of Christ or on mission.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published with C as the original key at a medium tempo. Check the refrain against the room before choosing a key.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The same two-line refrain follows each verse and doubles at the close, each time returning to Christ as Lord of all after a new part of his story.
communal.assessment: Congregational in form and in voice: a steady hymn-shaped melody with a refrain the whole room can carry.

strengths.title: Christ is named and described
strengths.explanation: Each verse speaks to Christ and says what he has done, so the addressee and the content are never unclear.

clarity.assessment: Clear. The language of Word, incarnation and intercession is biblical and teachable; nothing invites a wrong reading.

synthesis.summary: A hymn addressed to Christ as the eternal Word and creator, following his incarnation, humility and suffering for the guilty, then his rising, ascension and intercession, and the gathering of sinners from every nation. The refrain confesses him Lord of all. Nothing in it is wrong; the Spirit is not reached and the cross is told briefly.

scriptureReferences.relevance: The Word through whom all things were made - verse one.
All things created and held together in Christ.
The Son's humility and descent to the cross - verse two.
Redeemed people from every tribe and nation.
